### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **112** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**45** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 33 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2db2bac9f2dc19ac9b397963f575f8e5c3611c88` — the merge of head `40e6b5d6d75908b295545c97f414f9affc117088` into base `ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2db2bac9f2dc19ac9b397963f575f8e5c3611c88 && git checkout 2db2bac9f2dc19ac9b397963f575f8e5c3611c88
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd 40e6b5d6d75908b295545c97f414f9affc117088 && git checkout -B drift-repro ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd && git merge --no-ff 40e6b5d6d75908b295545c97f414f9affc117088

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ee3ae0360dc5beff655e4feb8f9624c731e306fd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb6012af863b02f48509305cebdb23b451a68b94`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #15206 (body and all 45 comments; bound to the stage plan 6067844889, stage 0's S5 row 6067752061, triage's Q2 B / Q3 A 6068032120 and Q1 → C 6073941543, S4's review 6090242635 and the S5 claim 6092019285; the S5 os-dev-report 6094700038); #22011 (body and its ruling A, 6020163868); the 2026-08-24 permission-set ruling as `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts`, `packaged-permission-set-overlay-detection.ts` and ADR-0126 record it on `main`; ADR-0131 D6, D7, D10 and ADR-0087 (D2 and the disposition addenda), read on `main` at `86da194919`; PR #22628 (body, its 71-file list, its one comment — the docs-drift note — and the net diff against its merge base: 71 files, +1,708 / −4,419, equal to the file list); the 35 check-runs on the head, all `completed`. Source on `main` read for the predicates the diff leans on (`isSealedManagedItem`, `registryAllowsOverlay`, `isArtifactShippedHook` / `isArtifactShippedAction`, the two projection gates' `--check`, the regeneration registry and `.gitattributes`). Nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head, as read.** Every required context is `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` (the leg carrying `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:migration-registry`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:objectql-double-limit` and `check:where-matcher`), `TypeScript Type Check` and its four legs (`· source gates` runs `check:authorable-surface`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide` and `check:docs`), `Test Core` and all six shards, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (rollup and 1/3 to 3/3), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also green: `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, the docs-link and docs-flag checks and the four claim and closing guards; `Console Pin Gate` and the packed-tarball smoke skipped by contract. The combined status is `success` (one external context). Not governed: no path under `.claude/`, `docs/adr/`, `skills/`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; head repo is the base repo; draft, `auto_merge` unset, read mergeable by GitHub. Size: 6,127 changed lines over 71 files — over `HUMAN_MERGE_LINE_THRESHOLD` (3000 on `main`) and over the 5,000 of AGENTS.md §7(c) — the human-merge route the body names; the route is the seat's.

**Every read that stops serving a row, each read off the net diff and judged.**

1. **The served-row resolution is one rule, environment only.** `servedOverlayRowCandidates` loses its organization scope (`legacyOrganizationId` is the one optional arm, below); `findServedOverlayRow` reads `organization_id IS NULL` rows only and no longer returns a scope; `getOverlayRepo()` takes no argument and is the environment singleton, with `legacyOrganizationRepo(id)` kept for exactly one caller, S4's uninstall removal (`removeLegacyOrganizationRowOnUninstall`, unchanged in effect). RIGHT: the stage plan's S5 row, D6 ("environment → code"), D7. The 20-case pin `protocol.reads-environment-only.test.ts` §1 drives five tier-A types × two caller shapes through item, list, layered, history, diff, audit, drafts, commits, lock and ETag; the dev's reverse verification (10 red with the `organization_id` predicate dropped, restored blob-equal) is the recorded direction, and `Test Core (3/6)` ran it green.
2. **Item, list, layered, cached.** `getMetaItem` / `getMetaItemLayered` / `getMetaItemCached` / `getMetaItems` lose `organizationId`; `readFlattenedMetaItems`' two-scope union and its draft-preview arm become one environment read (`queryDrafts(null, …)` only); the overlay cache key is `[type, packageId]`; the layered `overlay` layer is the environment row and `overlayScope` is `'env'` or `null`; the ETag validator is locale plus content, so one validator per item for every caller. RIGHT. The S4-carried residue — `organizationId` spread into the authoring gate, `MetadataAuthoringGateContext.organizationId`, `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules`' organization input and `foldStoredCollection`'s second scope — is deleted, not re-plumbed.
3. **History, diff, audit, drafts, commits.** `historyMetaItem` and `diffMetaItem` read the environment lineage; `auditMetaItem` builds `organization_id: null` unconditionally (the #8747 scope is kept, narrowed); `listDrafts` and `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` list `organization_id IS NULL` drafts and drop the per-draft `organizationId`; `packageScopedRowWhere` loses its organization parameter (not exported from the entry); `listCommits` is `{ package_id, organization_id: null }` for every caller, so `rollbackToPackageCommit`'s plan can no longer contain a legacy organization commit. RIGHT, and the trade S4 ①5 recorded is closed the consistent way: the whole-timeline read that showed an organization-active operator every organization's legacy commits is gone, and the legacy commits are counted in the boot report instead (item 7). `revertCommit` of a legacy commit stays `403` by S4's gate, as the dev notes.
4. **The `_lock` gate, search, diagnostics, references, version tokens, credential carry-forward.** `getEffectiveLock` / `readLockGateOverlayLayer` / `overlayLockLayerAt` / `resolveOverlayLockLayer` read the environment rows (`ITEM_ADDRESS_FIELDS` and `ItemAddress` lose `organizationId`, `StoredOverlayRowReader` loses its scope parameter — all internal to the package, not entry exports); `searchAll`'s page sweep, `getMetaDiagnostics`, `findReferencesToMeta`, `readVersionToken`, `restoredCredentialPathsFor`, `collectBatchPendingDeclarations` and `publishPackageDrafts`' pre-publish active-row read are environment reads. RIGHT.
5. **The new decline arm.** `declinesStoredRow` gains `isUnservedSealedOverlay(type, name)` = `isSealedManagedItem` minus `permission`. On `main`, `isSealedManagedItem` is `isArtifactBacked(type, name) && !registryAllowsOverlay(type)`, and `registryAllowsOverlay` is the `allowOrgOverride` set — the five regime-O types. So the arm declines an environment row over ANY item a code package ships whose type is not one of the five: the flow, action, hook, object and datasource the body names, and equally a managed `page`, `app`, `dataset` or `book` (the #6960 merge-at-read class that stage 0 noted as still merging over a managed artifact; the re-premised `protocol-registry-shadow` pin now serves the packaged `app`'s label over the stored row). RIGHT, on two grounds: Q1 → C defines the population as "overlay rows on sealed items", and the dev takes the seal's own predicate so the write refusal and the read narrowing cannot disagree; and D6 recognises no regime for such a row. The reach is wider than the body's examples and is stated here so nobody reads "flow, action, hook, object" as the whole class. The permission carve-out is judged in ③ Q1. The three objectql binders are not a gap: `isArtifactShippedHook` / `isArtifactShippedAction` already skip an authored row whose name a code package ships (artifact-wins), so the package definition wins at execution as well as at read. Pinned: §2 of the new pin (managed action and hook declined; the authored control served; a regime-O `view` overlay served; a permission fork served), and the dev's second ablation (2 red with the arm dropped).
6. **Boot hydration.** `loadMetaFromDb` keeps `organization_id IS NULL`; an `object` row that is a sealed overlay is not loaded (it would register as the layer ADR-0029 D9 makes the engine resolve the object through), and the read-side hydration in `readFlattenedMetaItems` skips the same rows; every other sealed type still hydrates its bare copy, which the reads decline (the #20913 shape, unchanged). RIGHT — judged in ③ Q2. The re-premised dogfood case (`showcase-object-extension-scalar-divergence`) pins exactly this: the pre-seal rename stays at rest and shows under `?layers=true`, item and list serve the package's label, boot names the row; `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green.
7. **The two boot reports.** `[metadata_org_scoped_unserved]` replaces `[metadata_org_scoped_unhydrated]` (the old token survives only in release-owned CHANGELOGs): type-blind, active and draft rows, the JS re-check of `organization_id`, a capped sample per type, plus a count of the legacy rows of `sys_metadata_commit` / `_history` / `_audit`, naming `os migrate` and that nothing is deleted or rewritten; `[metadata_sealed_overlay_unserved]` lists the sealed overlays per type with the two remedies Q1 → C names (a linkage-free clone, or delete the row). Both at `warn`: a functional degradation an operator can see (the customised behaviour is gone, the package's or the environment's is served), nothing claimed persisted is lost — the right level under AGENTS.md's one question. Both inside the diagnostic's own catch, so neither can become the outage (pinned: the probe-failure case). RIGHT, with one carried note: the three ledger counts are `find`s with no `limit` whose rows are loaded only to be counted; on a `single` deployment every pre-S3 Studio save left an organization-scoped audit row, so this is an unbounded read at every boot — a `count`, or a measured page, is the shape (③). Pinned in the re-premised `protocol.org-scoped-cold-boot-audit` suite and §3 of the new pin.
8. **objectql.** `readAuthoredHookRows`, `readAuthoredActionRows` and the object-rows arm skip a row with a non-empty `organization_id` (a row-value check, `isLegacyOrganizationRow`, as the federated-readers gate requires). RIGHT: stage 0's carried finding, the binders now follow the reads' rule; the legacy rows are in the type-blind boot report.
9. **The form doors (Q3 A).** `resolveFormBySlug` and `findPublicFormView` keep reading the Default Organization's legacy `view` layer: the rest door sends `legacyFormOrganizationId` in place of `organizationId`; the protocol honours it in `readFlattenedMetaItems` for `canonicalMetaType(type) === 'view'` alone (`readActiveOverlayRows` merges that organization's rows over the environment's, uncached, the organization's row winning its slot), and `findServedOverlayRow` never sees it, so the by-name read is untouched. The doors' `object` read becomes the environment's. No spec request declares the key, and no public door forwards a raw request object into `getMetaItems` — the runtime dispatcher and every REST door build typed literals — so the key is reachable in-process only. RIGHT; judged as a spelling in ③ Q3. Pinned on both sides: `public-form-withdrawal.test.ts` (every read's `organizationId` undefined, the two `view` reads `[ORG, undefined]` per door, FORM_NOT_FOUND and fail-closed cases unchanged) and §4 of the new pin (the key reaches no other type); the three withdrawal dogfood files are green.
10. **plugin-security and runtime.** `projectPermissionMutation`'s layered read names no organization (it reads what every reader reads), `permission-set-overlay-discard.ts` and the write-through drop the key; `domains/packages.ts` changes comments only. RIGHT.
11. **Spec (narrowing).** `organizationId` leaves `GetMetaItems`, `GetMetaItem`, `GetMetaItemLayered`, `AuditMetaItem`, `HistoryMetaItem` and `GetMetaItemCached` requests and each `ListDraftsResponse` draft; `overlayScope` is `z.enum(['env']).nullable()`. None of the request schemas is `.strict()`, so a request literal still carrying the key is stripped at a spec parse and reads the environment; the response schema now refuses `'org'` — which no server emits after this head. `authorable-surface/api.json` loses the six lines by hand (the vanished-key route S4 took; `Type Check · source gates` and `Spec property liveness` are green), `protocol.mdx` is regenerated with the schemas (`check:docs` green), and the `GetMetaItemResponse.version` and lock descriptions no longer name an organization partition. RIGHT. objectui at the pin: the dev reports the `LAYER_SCOPE_ZH` `org` key and four fixtures that will break on the next spec bump (carrier C9); whether objectui reads `drafts[].organizationId` is NOT MEASURED here (no objectui input in this review) — the bump owner reads it.
12. **metadata-core.** `meta-write-org-scope.ts` and its test are deleted and the entry export removed: `declaresOrgOverride` and `organizationIdForMetaRead` had no caller left (`TypeScript Type Check` green). RIGHT; a published removal, in the changeset.
13. **Published text against the code.** The changeset's "What changes" and FROM → TO rows each hold against the diff; the ADR-0087 entry's `surface` / `replacement` / `acceptanceCriteria` match the pin and the reports; `metadata-lifecycle.mdx`'s D6 callout now says the protocol refuses and every read is environment → code (S4's carried sentence), with a new sealed-overlay paragraph that names the permission exception; `metadata-service.mdx` is aligned; the `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` row of `environment-variables.mdx` turns "still served" into "kept at rest but not served" with the boot token and the remedies. One sentence of that row is left imprecise by item 5: "A row of a type that merges overlays at read (`permission`, `position`, `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `book`, `tool`, `skill`) can still be removed" — the removal door (`mergesOverlayAtRead`, read by `deleteMetaItem` alone) is intact, but after this head only `permission` still merges such a row at read; the other seven are declined. The operative claim holds; the characterisation is carried (③).

**Nothing is deleted or rewritten.** No added line in the diff calls a store write or delete (`insert`, `update`, `delete`, `put`, `restoreVersion`, `promoteDraft`); the one organization-scoped write left in the class is S4's uninstall removal, which this diff only renames the accessor of. The `sys_metadata` family's objects and `overlay-index.ts` are not in the file list.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15206-reads-environment-only.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/spec` — all six published, each with a behaviour or type narrowing in the diff; a title with `!`; a BREAKING (narrowing) paragraph; a FROM → TO table covering the six spec request keys, the five protocol request keys, the drafts member, `overlayScope: 'org'`, the two metadata-core exports, `MetadataAuthoringGateContext.organizationId`, the legacy organization row and the sealed overlay. The level is right: Changesets is in pre mode with tag `next`, the fixed group is already majored by the line's opening marker, S1 to S4 on this card are the precedent, and `Check Changeset` is green. Owing nothing: `@objectstack/runtime` (comments only), `@objectstack/dogfood` (private), `@objectstack/cli` (tests only). Two published type narrowings the table does not name — `projectPermissionMutation`'s `evt` parameter (exported from plugin-security's entry) and `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts`' row shape (the class is exported; the drafts row covers it in substance) — are inside packages the changeset already bumps with the BREAKING arm; the gate judges the claim made, so this is a note for the seat, not a ground.

ADR-0087: one marker, `registered metadata-read-organization-scope-retired`, in the gate's grammar; the entry exists under `migrations/entries/semantic/18.*` and `registry.ts` on the net diff is that one entry, byte-equal to its source (`check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:migration-registry` are `Lint & Repo Gates` steps, green). The kind is right: `semantic/`, because no authorable key is tombstoned (the six vanished keys take the no-tombstone route S4 took) and the read's old answer has no lossless mapping. **The committed projection `packages/spec/spec-changes.json` at this head does not carry the new id** (S4's two ids: 2 hits each; this one: 0). That is not a gate miss to argue with: `check:spec-changes` generates in memory and compares no committed copy by design (the publish lane generates the shipped one and verifies it from the tarball), so `check:generated --fix`'s "15/15 up to date" cannot see it. The committed copy is a `merge=os-regen` artifact, so one `gen:spec-changes` on the tree, committed alone, is a pure regeneration that stays under this record (③). `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` is not owed: it left the generated set at #22483 and nothing regenerates it (its full-guide shape on `main` is a pre-existing inconsistency, noted below); `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/**` is gitignored build output.

**`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`** on PR body line 2, in the changeset and on the claim 6092019285 — matches the diff. `no`: no read that is refused today is admitted — every change above removes a row from an answer, a key from a request, a value from an enum, a binding from a boot; the one new key, `legacyFormOrganizationId`, reproduces for `view` alone the reach `organizationId` already gave the two form doors, in-process only. `(narrowing)`: the BREAKING arm names what leaves. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations and open questions, from the S5 report 6094700038, each answered:
- **deviations.** Two post-push corrections (the seal's reach worded as every non-overlay type, not four named ones; the registry regenerated with it) and one dogfood case re-premised under Q1 → C: process, accepted; the re-premised case is item ①6's evidence, not a weakened pin.
- **Q1 (permission carve-out) → A, confirmed.** The 2026-08-24 maintainer ruling on existing permission-set forks is specific and standing: a detection reading plus the operator's Discard Overlay, "no automatic reap/merge … not a silent migration". Declining a stored fork at read would change the grants a deployment enforces with no operator act — the effect the ruling refused — and triage's Q1 → C named flow, action, hook and object, not permission sets. The carve-out is the one place the read narrowing and the seal's write refusal differ, and that asymmetry is the ruling's own shape (lock the base; existing forks reported, discarded by hand). The body's 维护者速读 puts the question in front of the maintainer for the human merge, which is the right place for a reversal if one comes.
- **Q2 (a sealed `object` overlay is not loaded at boot; other sealed types hydrate a bare copy) → A, confirmed.** An `object` row is the one type whose hydration changes the engine's effective schema (ADR-0029 D9's layer), so not loading it is what makes "the package definition wins" true for the engine, not only for `/meta`; every other type's bare copy is declined at read by the existing #20913 shape, and the dev measured B (skip every sealed type) reddening the flow-shipped-name pins the bare copy carries. ADR-0029 D9 is not reversed in general — ADR-0131 D6, the later accepted record, seals the managed object the overlay would layer over; the dated note on ADR-0029 D9 that triage's Q1 → C assigned to S7 (Tier H) is still owed there. A registry-direct `getItem` on a bare copy of a non-object sealed type is the pre-existing #20913 exposure, not new.
- **Q3 (`legacyFormOrganizationId` as a protocol-internal key) → A, confirmed.** The only callers are the two anonymous form doors; the read retires with C7's carry (Q3 A, #22008 A); declaring the key in `@objectstack/spec` would publish a request member for a read that is scheduled to leave; no public door forwards a raw request object, and the pin shows the key reaches no other type.
- **Carried from S4 ③, each closed here:** the authoring-gate spread and `MetadataAuthoringGateContext.organizationId` (deleted); the seed loader's `config.organizationId` prescription (now `organization_id` on the record first, the publish path named); `listCommits`' organization branch and the door's whole-timeline read (environment only, legacy commits counted at boot); `metadata-lifecycle.mdx`'s D6 callout (says the protocol refuses and the reads are environment → code); Zone 2 (`getOverlayRepo` is one environment repository; the repository's `organizationId` option stays for the uninstall removal alone; `stored-migration.ts` keeps `organizationId` on the migration row only to describe the row S4's `skipped` report names — not a read, accepted); S4 ①8's two uninstall residue classes are the population the type-blind boot report now names (their fate is C7's); the runtime suites whose names still say org-scope now pin environment-wide behaviour (churn, as S4 said). From S3's review: the per-organization overlay wording is rewritten. From stage 0: the hook and action binders.
- **The claim's ⛔ Not list holds:** the anonymous form doors' organization-layer withdrawal read is kept (①9); no stored row is deleted or rewritten (①, last paragraph); no column or index work on the `sys_metadata` family (no such file in the diff).
- **Undeclared cross-lane paths.** The report's `cross_lane_paths` list (rest, runtime, plugin-security, spec, dogfood, docs and the two script ledgers) is longer than the claim's dispatch-time declaration (it adds the dogfood case, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` and `scripts/objectql-double-limit.baseline.json`, and the runtime and rest test files by name); whether each is on its lane post before the PR leaves draft is outside this review's inputs — **escalated** to the seat, as in S4.

For the seat before the landing (none a verdict ground):
- **Regenerate `packages/spec/spec-changes.json`** (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:spec-changes`) on this tree and commit it alone, with a `Regen-provenance:` line on the PR naming this record, the old head and the new one — a pure regeneration, so this record carries to that head. `main` is past this head's merge base; if the landing merges `main` first, use `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` and run `check:generated --fix`, then regenerate the manifest — `check:generated` cannot see its staleness.
